name: Causal Forest (DML)
tagline: Generalized random forest CATE estimator with double-machine-learning residualization (econml CausalForestDML).
pseudocode:
1. Cross-fit nuisance: $\hat m(X)=E[Y|X]$ via GBR, $\hat e(X)=E[T|X]$ via GBR
2. Residualize: $\tilde Y=Y-\hat m(X)$, $\tilde T=T-\hat e(X)$
3. Fit GeneralizedRandomForest on residuals with honest splitting (n_estimators=500, min_samples_leaf=5, cv=3)
4. Predict: $\hat\tau(x) = \text{forest.effect}(x)$
5. Sklearn fallback: manual KFold residualization, R-Learner pseudo-outcome with weights $\tilde T^2$, fit RandomForestRegressor
diff_from_baseline: Athey, Tibshirani & Wager 2019, Annals of Statistics (originally Wager & Athey 2018, JASA). Combines DML (Chernozhukov et al. 2018) with honest random forests for heterogeneous CATE; default tree-based CATE benchmark.

name: DR-Learner
tagline: Doubly-robust meta-learner: combines outcome and propensity models via cross-fit pseudo-outcomes, then regresses on X.

key_hyperparams.name: pseudo clip
key_hyperparams.role: trim heavy tails before final fit

diff_from_baseline: Kennedy 2023 (EJS); Chernozhukov et al. 2018. Doubly-robust pseudo-outcome consistent if either nuisance model is correct. Standard CATE meta-learner; uses GradientBoosting for $\mu_0,\mu_1,e$ and the final $\tau$ regression.

name: IPW
tagline: Horvitz-Thompson inverse-propensity reweighting, then regress weighted pseudo-outcome on X for CATE.
diff_from_baseline: Horvitz & Thompson 1952; Hirano, Imbens & Ridder 2003 (Econometrica). Reweights observations by inverse propensity to remove selection bias, then fits an outcome model. Classical baseline for ATE/CATE estimation.

name: R-Learner
tagline: Robinson-decomposition meta-learner: regress Y residual on T residual times tau(X) with weights $\tilde T^2$.
formula: $$\hat\tau = \arg\min_\tau \sum_i \big(Y_i-\hat m(X_i)\big) - \big(T_i-\hat e(X_i)\big)\,\tau(X_i)\big)^2,\quad \text{equivalently use pseudo } \tilde Y_i/\tilde T_i \text{ with weight } \tilde T_i^2$$
diff_from_baseline: Nie & Wager 2021 (Biometrika). Uses Robinson (1988) residualization for orthogonal CATE estimation; quasi-oracle rate independent of nuisance estimation rate. Standard CATE baseline.

name: S-Learner
tagline: Single regression model with treatment as a feature; CATE = predict(X,T=1) - predict(X,T=0).
diff_from_baseline: Kunzel et al. 2019 (PNAS). Simplest meta-learner: a single outcome model trained on stacked (X,T). Default starting baseline; can underestimate CATE if treatment effect is small relative to feature signal.

name: T-Learner
tagline: Two separate outcome models, one per treatment arm; CATE = mu1(X) - mu0(X).
diff_from_baseline: Kunzel et al. 2019 (PNAS). Two-model baseline; works well when treatment groups are balanced but suffers under propensity overlap issues. Standard CATE meta-learner.
